newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary MHB bank sees privatisation, profit growth.
newsitem.headline: Hungary MHB bank sees privatisation, profit growth.

text.p: Hungary's Magyar Hitel Bank (MHB), awaiting privatisation, will raise profits this year and forge ahead with modernisation, General Manager Zsigmond Jarai told journalists on Friday.
The state privatisation agency APV has recently published a one-round private tender for the sale of an 89.23 percent stake in MHB, Hungary's fifth largest bank. @

MHB said in a statement that it posted an after-tax profit of 3.44 billion forints in the first eight months of this year, compared with a four billion forint target for 1996 and 1.4 billion forints after-tax profit in 1995.
"Our after-tax profit will be between four and five billion forints this year," Jarai said, adding the bank will not slow down its modernisation programme despite being very close to privatisation.
The three banks invited to the privatisation tender can submit their bids until October 17, Jarai said. @
According to press reports, the three banks are Austria's Creditanstalt-Bankverein CABV-pa.VI, Bank Austria-Girocredit and the Dutch ABN Amro Bank NV.
Creditanstalt, which already has a banking subsidiary in Hungary, said earlier on Friday that it wants to fuse its Hungarian operations if it succeeds in buying MHB.

Jarai said Bank of America pulled out saying the tender did not leave enough time for it to do a due dilligence at MHB, but the U.S. bank said it would be interested in MHB's sale again if the current tender should prove unsuccessful. @
Jarai said MHB was forging ahead with a programme of cost cutting and expansion in retail financial services.
MHB plans to specialise 40 of its branches in retail banking, by setting up a subsidiary, MHB Nepbank next year.
The remaining 30 brances will specialise in corporate clients. MHB is likely to set up a new branch in Szeged, South Hungary. Jarai added.
The bank also plans to set up a life and pension insurance company with a registered capital of 2.1 billion forints in early 1997. @
Jarai said he would undertake leading the bank after the privatisation if the buyer continues the bank's modernisation programme. He added he believed that the potential buyers support MHB's plans.
He also said he was sure that the rating agency Moody's Investors Service will upgrade MHB in its next report about the bank as MHB significantly improved its performance this year.

Moody's said recently that MHB received the worst rating of five large Hungarian banks, but the agency only repeated what it had said in April in a report based on the 1995 activities of the banks, Jarai said. @
MHB received Ba3 rating for its long-term deposits, Not Prime for short-term deposits and E+ for financial strength.
